problems.title: Supergeometric approximation on sparse degrees does not force entire extension

location.proof: p33, subsequence replaced by consecutive degrees

problems.claim: For nonextendible f, some D>1 forces error>C/D^n for every sufficiently large n and every C>0/admissible sequence.
assumptions_checked: K=closed unit disk has positive capacity1; P={infinity} is exactly one point in the sole complementary component.
f=sum_{j>=2}(z/2)^(j!) is holomorphic on |z|<2, a neighborhood of K, and unbounded as real z approaches2; hence no entire extension.
R_n contains precisely terms j!<=n, degree<=n and poles only at infinity.
problems.decisive_check: At n=k!, error<=2^(1-(k+1)!). For every D>1, D^(k!)*error<=2 exp(k![logD-(k+1)log2])->0. This violates every candidate lower bound infinitely often.
problems.core_dependency: False Theorem8.1 and introductory sharpness claim. In the subsequence proof, pole degree is n_(k+1), not n_k+1, so D1^(n_(k+1))*D^(-n_k) need not be summable.
problems.impact_rationale: Announced sharpness theorem is disproved under all stated hypotheses.
problems.repair_candidate: Require upper estimates at all sufficiently large degrees for the consecutive-degree extension argument; only a limsup obstruction follows in the disk/polynomial case.
problems.repair_boundary: No general corrected theorem for arbitrary P/irregular K certified. Does not refute TheoremA or TheoremB's existence upper bound.
counterevidence: K is not a finite or polar set.
The full sequence R_n is defined; only its especially accurate subsequence is used.
Failure is not caused by poles outside the allowed set.

independent_acceptance.source_claim_and_location: Theorem8.1, PDF32, requires a geometric lower bound at every sufficiently large degree for every admissible approximation sequence. PDF33 explicitly replaces an arbitrary subsequence n_k by consecutive n in its proof. The subsequence extension claim is also announced on PDF4.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: K is the closed unit disk of capacity1, its spherical complement has one component, P={infinity}, U={|z|<2}, and f=sum_(j>=2)(z/2)^(j!). The truncations over j!<=n are polynomials of degree<=n with poles only at the prescribed point. f is holomorphic on U but diverges on the real radius approaching2 and therefore has no entire extension.
independent_acceptance.decisive_independent_check: At n=k!, the uniform tail on K is at most sum_(m>=(k+1)!)2^-m=2^(1-(k+1)!). Multiplication by any fixed D^(k!) gives at most2 exp(k![log D-(k+1)log2]), tending to0. For every D>1 and every C>0, infinitely many degrees therefore violate the asserted lower bound. The counterexample fulfills each theorem premise.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundaries: This refutes the all-large-degree lower bound and the supergeometric-subsequence extension assertion. It does not contradict TheoremB's existence of some geometric upper rate or TheoremA's approximation conclusion.
independent_acceptance.severity_result: Major retained: an announced sharpness theorem is false in the basic disk/polynomial case.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: For sparse degrees the local pole order of R_(n_(k+1))-R_(n_k) is bounded by n_(k+1), not n_k+1; the controlling product D1^(n_(k+1)) D^(-n_k) need not decay. A hypothesis covering every sufficiently large degree supports the consecutive-degree argument where its Green setup applies; only the corresponding disk/polynomial limsup-rate distinction is checked, not a general corrected theorem.

problems.title: Repeated zeros supply fewer interpolation conditions than counted
problems.claim: Jets of orders0..n-1 at each distinct zero determine the degree<=dn-1 approximant with fixed poles/orders.
assumptions_checked: K disk radius1/2, P=infinity,U disk radius3,f=z,r=z^2,d2,n1.
R4,rho3 yield C_R radius2 and valid levels1 and4/3.
Computed R1=z and alternative2z have degree1 and the same order-one pole at infinity.
problems.decisive_check: Both satisfy the sole printed condition R(0)=f(0)=0, but z!=2z.
problems.core_dependency: Fails interpolation uniqueness; source explicitly says proposition is not needed for TheoremB.
problems.repair_candidate: At a zero of multiplicity m_a impose jets0..n*m_a-1. Error formula vanishes to that order and total nd conditions imply uniqueness with fixed pole divisor.
problems.repair_boundary: Multiplicity correction verified for the stated finite-zero setup; no claim that an unstated simple-zero construction was used.
counterevidence: Same poles and same orders hold, so different pole divisors do not explain nonuniqueness.
